changes.title: fix: refuse a shallow clone instead of reading it as a first release
changes.description:
Closes #243

- **Checked where the range start is resolved:** `GitCliCommitReader` asks `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` right after the tag resolves. The reader runs first in the pipeline, so the refusal comes before any GitHub request or model call.
- **No start named in a shallow clone is refused,** whatever the previous-tag lookup would find. The clone's history ends at the fetch depth, which reads exactly like a first tag's history ending at the root, and a previous tag found inside the depth may still not be the nearest one. The message says the clone is shallow and names the three fixes: `git fetch --unshallow --tags`, `fetch-depth: 0`, `GIT_DEPTH: 0`.
- **`--whole-history` is refused by the same check:** it reaches the reader with no start, and the history it would render is not the whole history. `WholeHistoryException` is never reached in a shallow clone, so the "first tag" advice that sent users to `--whole-history` no longer appears there.
- **`--since <ref>` still runs in a shallow clone,** so a deliberately limited fetch is not blocked. It is refused with the fix when:
  - the ref is not in the fetched history ("is not in the fetched history of this shallow clone", instead of "does not resolve");
  - the fetched history does not connect it to the tag (not an ancestor *in the fetched history*; the connecting commits may be missing);
  - a commit from git's `shallow` file lies inside `since..tag`: the start is connected along main, but a merged branch older than the depth is cut off, so commits of the release are missing. This is conservative: a boundary commit whose real parent is the start itself is refused too, since git hides that parent and the unshallow fix covers it.
- **The fix text lives in the git adapter,** next to the existing `git fetch --tags` hint, not in the CLI: it is about how the clone was made, not about Chartula's flags.
- Docs: README gains an "In CI" section with `fetch-depth: 0` and `GIT_DEPTH: 0` (there was no CI snippet for checkout before); `docs/cli.md` gets "A shallow clone" under "Where a release starts"; the `IReleaseCommitReader` exception doc names the case.

**Reproduced before the fix**, the issue's steps on a real shallow clone of this repository, binary built from main:

```
$ git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula.git && cd chartula
$ git fetch --depth 1 origin tag v0.1.0-preview.1
$ git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository
true
$ chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --repo goldbarth/chartula
Error: v0.1.0-preview.1 is the first tag, so its range is the whole history (1 commits).
  Rendered as it is, that reads as a development log rather than a release.
  --since <ref>     start the release after a tag or commit (e.g. the last state you shipped)
  --whole-history   render all of it, e.g. for a project whose history is the release
[exit code: 1]
```
After `git fetch --unshallow --tags` the same tag has 100 commits. (`v0.1.0-preview.1` is in fact this repository's only tag, so the "predecessor beyond the depth" case is reproduced in the tests below, on local shallow clones.)

**Verified after the fix**, same clone, binary from this branch:

```
$ chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --repo goldbarth/chartula      # and with --whole-history: identical
Error: The checkout is a shallow clone: its history ends at the fetch depth, not where 'v0.1.0-preview.1' starts, so neither the previous tag nor the whole history can be read from it.
  Fetch the full history and tags: git fetch --unshallow --tags
  In GitHub Actions, check out with fetch-depth: 0; in GitLab CI, set GIT_DEPTH: 0.
[exit code: 1]

$ chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --repo goldbarth/chartula --since v0.0.0-nope
Error: The release start 'v0.0.0-nope' is not in the fetched history of this shallow clone.
  Fetch the full history and tags: git fetch --unshallow --tags
  In GitHub Actions, check out with fetch-depth: 0; in GitLab CI, set GIT_DEPTH: 0.
[exit code: 1]
```

Tests: against real shallow clones (`git clone --depth N` over `file://`, via `TempGitRepository.ShallowClone`): `GitCliCommitReaderTests` (refused without a start; `--since` fetched with the tag reads the range; start not fetched; start not connected; range cut off inside by a merged branch) and `ShallowCloneTests` (the built CLI, with and without `--whole-history`: exit 1, the fixes named, no "first tag", no GitHub request). The six refusal tests fail on main. Full suite 813 passing, build without warnings, `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat: install and run Chartula on Alpine (musl), checked in every mainstream Linux
changes.description:
Closes #240. Follows #241 (no ICU), which the glibc containers below need.

**Musl binaries**
- `linux-musl-x64` and `linux-musl-arm64` join `RuntimeIdentifiers`; the six `packages.lock.json` files gain the two (empty) runtime sections, so the release's locked restore passes. No package changes.
- Published from the glibc runners: a self-contained, non-AOT binary needs only the musl runtime pack, which the restore brings.
- **The binary jobs move to `binaries.yml`** (`workflow_call`), unchanged apart from the two new platforms and the container smoke test. `release.yml` calls it and releases what it built; `install.yml` calls it to install the binaries a pull request builds. One definition of how a shipped binary is built, not two. The binary jobs are not required checks, so the new job names (`binary / binary (<rid>)`) break no ruleset.
- **Smoke tests run where users run:** the musl binaries in `alpine:latest` with only `libstdc++` added, the glibc ones in `debian:12-slim`. The runner has ICU and every library a slim image lacks, so smoke-testing on it would not have caught #239.
- Docs: `docs/versioning.md` (release assets, how a release is made).

**install.sh**
- **Detects musl by its loader** (`/lib/ld-musl-*.so.1`, then `ldd --version`) and downloads `chartula-linux-musl-<arch>`.
- **libstdc++ is checked before the download.** When it is missing, the script stops with `apk add libstdc++` (or "install libstdc++ with your package manager" without apk, "(as root)" when not root) and installs nothing. It never installs a package itself.
- **The PATH hint names a file the shell reads.** `$SHELL` is unset in most containers, so the hint used to fall back to `~/.profile`, which a non-login bash never reads. The shell is now `$SHELL`, else the script's parent from `/proc/$PPID/comm` - the shell the user typed `curl | sh` into. bash gets `~/.bashrc` (`~/.bash_profile` on macOS); `~/.profile` is left for shells that read nothing else.
- **The hint makes `chartula` work in this terminal:** `export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"` first, then the line that keeps it for new terminals.
- shellcheck clean.

**install.yml**
- **Linux container matrix:** ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:12-slim, fedora:latest, almalinux:8, almalinux:9, opensuse/leap:15.6, amazonlinux:2023, archlinux:latest and alpine:latest, on x64 and arm64 (Arch has no arm64 image): 19 jobs.
- **In each container:** only git and ca-certificates are installed. Ubuntu and Debian also get curl, because they ship neither curl nor wget, and the install line is `curl ... | sh`. Then `.github/scripts/check-install.sh`:
  - on Alpine, it first asserts that install.sh fails, prints `apk add libstdc++` and installs nothing; then it adds libstdc++;
  - it installs with install.sh and puts `chartula` on the PATH with the hint's own `export` line, so the hint is tested too;
  - it clones this repository and runs a real `chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --since 4bc57c8` against `https://api.openai.com/v1` with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy` and the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
  - Pass is exit 1 with `answered 401 Unauthorized`: git read the history, the GitHub API answered over TLS, and the model call went out, for no tokens.
- **macOS and Windows:** `--help` is replaced with the same run - check-install.sh on macOS, the same check in PowerShell on Windows (both shells).
- **What gets installed:** a pull request installs the binaries it builds (via `binaries.yml`, served over loopback with a `SHA256SUMS`, through install.sh's existing `CHARTULA_DOWNLOAD_URL`). A published release installs itself, as before.
- actionlint clean.

**README:** "No .NET is needed" is followed by the requirements: Linux with glibc or musl (Alpine: `apk add libstdc++`), macOS, Windows, and git. There is an Alpine CI snippet (`apk add --no-cache git libstdc++`, the install line with busybox `wget`, the `export`), and the musl files are in the download list.

**Reproduced before the change**, alpine:latest:

```
$ /b/chartula-linux-x64 --help            # the preview.1 glibc binary
sh: /b/chartula: not found
[exit code: 127]

$ sh install.sh                           # main
Error: this Linux uses musl (e.g. Alpine), and Chartula's Linux binaries need glibc. Build it from source: ...
[exit code: 1]

$ ./chartula-linux-musl-x64 --help        # without libstdc++
Error loading shared library libgcc_s.so.1: No such file or directory (needed by ./chartula-linux-musl-x64)
Error loading shared library libstdc++.so.6: No such file or directory (needed by ./chartula-linux-musl-x64)
[exit code: 127]
```

The PATH hint on ubuntu:24.04 with `$SHELL` unset (a new non-login bash still does not find `chartula` after following it):

```
Add it once with:
  echo 'export PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> /root/.profile
then open a new terminal.
```

**Verified after the change**, locally with the binaries this branch publishes (locked restore, `-warnaserror`), served over loopback. On alpine:latest, check-install.sh:

```
Error: Chartula needs libstdc++, which is not installed. Install it with:
  apk add libstdc++
then run this again. Nothing was installed.
Installing Chartula from http://127.0.0.1:8765 (linux-musl-x64) into /root/.local/bin
Installed and checked: /root/.local/bin/chartula

/root/.local/bin is not on your PATH yet, so the shell cannot find chartula.
Use it in this terminal now with:
  export PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"
and keep it for new terminals with:

...
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v0.1.0-preview.1' failed: openai-compatible at https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions answered 401 Unauthorized for model 'gpt-5.6-luna'.
...
  Release:          2 commits, 2 pull requests, 1 fact (1 with a description, 3,396 characters)
Passed: git, the GitHub API and the model endpoint were all reached.
```
The other nine images passed the same script (x64). The four Linux binaries passed the release smoke test in debian:12-slim and alpine:latest (arm64 under emulation). The PATH hint on ubuntu:24.04 with `$SHELL` unset now names `~/.bashrc`, and a new non-login bash finds `chartula` after following it:

```
Use it in this terminal now with:
  export PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"
and keep it for new terminals with:
  echo 'export PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> /root/.bashrc
--- a new non-login bash:
/root/.local/bin/chartula
```

**CI on this PR** ([Install](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/actions/runs/35878386916), [Release](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/actions/runs/35878387055), [CI](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/actions/runs/35878386456)): all green.

| | x64 | arm64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:12-slim | pass | pass |
| fedora:latest, almalinux:8, almalinux:9 | pass | pass |
| opensuse/leap:15.6, amazonlinux:2023 | pass | pass |
| archlinux:latest | pass | no image |
| alpine:latest (hint asserted, then installed) | pass | pass |
| macOS (macos-15-intel, macos-latest) | pass | pass |
| Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7 | pass | pass |

The eight binaries passed their smoke tests in `binaries.yml` (Linux in debian:12-slim and alpine:latest). On alpine:latest arm64:
```
Error: Chartula needs libstdc++, which is not installed. Install it with:
  apk add libstdc++
then run this again. Nothing was installed.
Installing Chartula from http://127.0.0.1:8000 (linux-musl-arm64) into /root/.local/bin
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v0.1.0-preview.1' failed: openai-compatible at https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions answered 401 Unauthorized for model 'gpt-5.6-luna'.
```

The first run failed on macOS and Windows for reasons in the workflow, fixed in the second commit to it:
- The loopback server was not up yet when macOS's curl asked; the Linux jobs only won the race because of the image pull. Each job now waits for it.
- `sh install.sh | tee` reported tee's status, so a failed install read as a passed one. The script now checks install.sh itself.
- On Windows the check passed, and the step then ended with chartula's own exit code (the expected 1). It now ends with `exit 0`.

Tests: no .NET code changes; full suite 806 passing under a locked restore, build clean; install.sh and check-install.sh shellcheck clean, workflows actionlint clean.

changes.title: fix: start without ICU, so the Linux binaries run in slim containers
changes.description:
Closes #239

- **`<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>` in `Chartula.Cli.csproj`:** the runtime no longer looks for ICU, so the binary starts where there is none - which is every slim container image except Arch. Before, it ended at startup with `FailFast` and a core dump.
- **Why Chartula does not need ICU:** ICU supplies culture data - linguistic comparison and casing, culture-specific number and date formats, IDN host names. Chartula uses none of it on purpose, because its output is a record that has to be the same wherever it runs:
  - every comparison and dictionary is ordinal (`StringComparison.Ordinal`/`OrdinalIgnoreCase`), every regex is `CultureInvariant`, casing is `ToLowerInvariant`;
  - numbers, durations and dates are formatted with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` (`N0`, `0.0`, `yyyy-MM-dd`), git dates parsed with it; every sort is by integer or enum;
  - it prints no text in the user's locale. What invariant mode changes - culture-aware comparison of ignorable characters, non-ASCII host names - is not something Chartula relies on; its endpoints are ASCII.
- **The tests run without ICU too:** the three test projects carry the same property, so the suite checks the output the shipped binary produces, not the output of a mode it never runs in.
- `GlobalizationTests`: the runtime configuration built next to the binary says `System.Globalization.Invariant: true`, and the tests themselves run in the invariant culture.

**Reproduced before the fix:** the v0.1.0-preview.1 linux-x64 binary (checked against `SHA256SUMS`) in fresh containers with only git and ca-certificates, running a real `chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --since 4bc57c8` on a clone of this repository, against `https://api.openai.com/v1` with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy`:

```
Process terminated.
Couldn't find a valid ICU package installed on the system. Please install libicu (or icu-libs) using your package manager and try again. ...
   at System.Environment.FailFast(...)
   ...
   at Chartula.Cli.Program.BuildConfiguration()
[exit code: 134]
```
on ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:12-slim, fedora:latest, almalinux:8, almalinux:9, opensuse/leap:15.6 and amazonlinux:2023; archlinux:latest ran. A binary built from main before this change crashed the same way.

**Verified after the fix,** same containers, same command, a linux-x64 binary published from this branch the way the release does (`--self-contained`, locked restore, `-warnaserror`):

| Image | glibc | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu:22.04 | 2.35 | 401 from the model endpoint, exit 1 |
| ubuntu:24.04 | 2.39 | 401, exit 1 |
| debian:12-slim | 2.36 | 401, exit 1 |
| fedora:latest | 2.43 | 401, exit 1 |
| almalinux:8 | 2.28 | 401, exit 1 |
| almalinux:9 | 2.34 | 401, exit 1 |
| opensuse/leap:15.6 | 2.38 | 401, exit 1 |
| amazonlinux:2023 | 2.34 | 401, exit 1 |
| archlinux:latest | 2.44 | 401, exit 1 |

The 401 is the pass: git read the history, the GitHub API answered over TLS (`Release: 2 commits, 2 pull requests, 1 fact`), and the model call went out, for no tokens:

```
--- Technical ---
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v0.1.0-preview.1' failed: openai-compatible at https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions answered 401 Unauthorized for model 'gpt-5.6-luna'.
           The endpoint rejected the key in OPENAI_API_KEY: it is expired, revoked or mistyped, or it is another provider's key.
```

**Output unchanged, shown by the fixture tests:** the full suite, fixture replays included (`FixturePipelineTests`, `FactBaseFixture`, `PromptSnapshotTests`), passes the same 804 tests without ICU and with ICU in three cultures - the replays compare with stored files byte for byte, so one differing character would fail them:

| Mode | Culture | Core / Infrastructure / Cli |
| --- | --- | --- |
| invariant (as shipped) | invariant | 452 / 68 / 284 |
| ICU (`-p:InvariantGlobalization=false`) | `C.UTF-8` | 452 / 68 / 284 |
| ICU | `de_DE.UTF-8` | 452 / 68 / 284 |
| ICU | `tr_TR.UTF-8` (checked: the test host ran as `tr-TR`) | 452 / 68 / 284 |

Musl (Alpine) binaries, the installer and a container matrix in CI follow in #240, stacked on this.

Tests: `GlobalizationTests` (binary and test hosts run without ICU); full suite 806 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: fix(config): refuse a malformed chartula.yaml naming the file, line and column
changes.description:
Closes #237

- **Read with positions, not deserialized to `object`:** `ChartulaYamlReader` loads the file through YamlDotNet's representation model, which keeps the line and column of every key and value (and is reflection-free, so no step back for the AOT goal). The flattening into `Chartula:` keys is unchanged.
- **Syntax errors become configuration errors:** file, line and column, YamlDotNet's reason without its `(Line: .., Col: .., Idx: ..)` prefix, and what it most likely means:
  - a line indented under a key that already has a value (the case in the issue) is named as such, with both lines and their indentation;
  - a line that lines up with no key above it names the levels that exist;
  - a tab is named on its own line - YamlDotNet reports line 1, column 1 for it;
  - an unclosed `[`/`{` says so; a duplicate key is refused instead of the last one winning silently.
- **Unknown keys are refused, not ignored:** binding drops a key it does not know, so `faithfulness:` indented under `llm:` - valid YAML once the 4-space lines are fixed - left `thorough: false` without effect. The refusal says what the key most likely is: a section of its own, a key of another section (`'model' is a key of 'llm' and 'faithfulness'`), or a misspelling (`Did you mean 'model'?`). Keys of maps the user names (`labels.category`, `categories.names`) are free.
- **Wrong shapes and types:** `true`/`false` keys take only those (the binder's message named `Chartula:Faithfulness:Thorough` and `System.Boolean`, and no line); list keys take a list, other keys a single value; a section takes keys. Values beyond that (`thinking`, `depth`, `maxOutputTokens`) are still checked where they are read, as before.
- **Schema by hand, held to the types:** `ChartulaYamlSchema` lists every key; `ChartulaYamlSchemaTests` fails when an options type gains a property the list does not have, or the reverse.
- **Unchanged:** an empty value, `~` or `null` still leaves the setting unset; keys are still case-insensitive; the environment-only refusal still comes first and reads as before. Every problem is named at once, one per line.
- Docs: `configuration.md` (A file that cannot be read as meant), `cli.md` (Configuration file).

**Reproduced before the fix** with the release binary, the file from the issue:

```
Unhandled exception. (Line: 3, Col: 10, Idx: 36) - (Line: 3, Col: 10, Idx: 36): YamlDotNet.Core.SemanticErrorException: While scanning a plain scalar value, found invalid mapping.
   at YamlDotNet.Core.Parser.ParseNode(Boolean isBlock, Boolean isIndentlessSequence, Boolean isKey)
   ...
[exit code: 134]
```
Tabs and an unclosed `[` crashed the same way; an unknown key, `faithfulness:` under `llm:`, a scalar for a list, a list for a scalar and a duplicate key ran with the setting silently not in force.

**Verified after the fix**, same file, exit code 1:

```
Configuration error: chartula.yaml, line 3, column 10: this is not valid YAML (While scanning a plain scalar value, found invalid mapping). Check the indentation: line 3 is indented further than line 2 (4 spaces against 2), but line 2 already has a value, so nothing can be nested under it. The keys of one section line up.
```
The other cases, each exit code 1:
```
chartula.yaml, line 4, column 3: this is not valid YAML (While parsing a block mapping, did not find expected key). Check the indentation: line 4 is indented 2 spaces, which lines up with no key above it (they are at 0 or 4). The keys of one section line up.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 1: this line is indented with a tab. YAML indents with spaces only.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 1: this is not valid YAML (While parsing a flow sequence, did not find expected ',' or ']'). Check that every '[' and '{' on it is closed.
chartula.yaml, line 4, column 3: 'faithfulness' is not a key of 'llm' but a section of its own. Check the indentation: 'faithfulness:' starts at the beginning of its line, like 'llm:'.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 3: unknown key 'modle' in 'llm'. Did you mean 'model'?
chartula.yaml, line 1, column 1: unknown key 'model' at the top level: it is a key of 'llm' and 'faithfulness'. Check the indentation: it belongs indented under its section.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 13: 'faithfulness.thorough' is 'maybe'; expected true or false.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 22: 'filter.excludeCategories' takes a list, such as [a, b], not the value 'Internal'.
chartula.yaml, line 2, column 10: 'llm.model' takes a single value, not a list.
chartula.yaml, line 3, column 1: 'llm' is set a second time here; the second would replace the first. Set it once.
```

Tests: `MalformedYamlTests` (every case above, all problems at once, file named as found, empty values and casing unchanged, the documented example and this repository's `chartula.yaml` accepted), `ChartulaYamlSchemaTests` (schema matches the options types), `MalformedConfigurationTests` (the built CLI on the issue's file: exit 1, no stack trace); full suite 775 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean. Merged together with #235 and #236: 804 passing.

changes.title: fix: name the provider, endpoint, model and status of a failed model call
changes.description:
Closes #234

- **Read off the wire, below both SDKs:** a handler under the provider clients (next to the request count from #229) keeps the last error response of the call in progress - address, status, the endpoint's own message. Both SDKs word their exceptions differently (`Status Code: NotFound` vs `HTTP 404 (...)`) and neither names the address; read here, they come out the same and no provider exception type is named.
- **Written where all three are known:** `FailureDescribingChatClient` wraps the provider client in the composition root, the one place that knows provider, endpoint and model. The domain still sees an exception with a message, so `ReleaseChangelogGenerator` is unchanged.
- **The message:** `<provider> at <address> answered <status> for model '<model>'.`, then what the status usually means, then `The endpoint said: ...`. The address is the one requested, which shows a doubled or missing `/v1`; query and user info are left out, since some providers take a key there.
  - `404`: the model id is not served (`check llm.model`), or `Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl` is not this provider's API. Without a base URL only the model is named - the endpoint is the provider's own.
  - `401`/`403`: names the key variable; a `401` with the variable unset (possible with `openai-compatible`) says so.
  - No answer at all: the configured endpoint and the transport's reason (`Connection refused (...)`), not the SDK's `I/O exception` around it.
- **Said once:** audiences that failed with the same text print it under the first and `The same as Technical.` under the rest. Continuation lines are indented under their audience instead of starting flush left.
- **A failed thorough check no longer crashes the run:** found while reproducing. With `faithfulness.model` set to a model the endpoint does not serve, the check's call threw out of the pipeline as an unhandled exception with a stack trace and a core dump, and the renderings were lost. It is now `NotEvaluated` with the same explanation, naming `faithfulness.model`; the rendering is kept and flagged, as for an unreadable verdict. Cancellation still propagates.
- Merges cleanly with #235 (#233), which touches another part of `LlmServiceCollectionExtensions`.
- Docs: `cli.md` (When a model call fails), `configuration.md` (the `401` sentence).

**Reproduced before the fix** with the release binary against a local stub (`Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl` pointed at it, dummy keys), both providers:

```
--- Technical ---

{"type": "error", "error": {"type": "not_found_error", "message": "model: claude-sonnet-5"}}

--- Customer ---
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v1.1.0' failed: Status Code: NotFound
{"type": "error", "error": {"type": "not_found_error", "message": "model: claude-sonnet-5"}}
```
```
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v1.1.0' failed: HTTP 401 (invalid_request_error: invalid_api_key)

Incorrect API key provided: sk-dummy.
```
and with the stub answering 404 only for the check's model:
```
Unhandled exception. Anthropic.Exceptions.AnthropicNotFoundException: Status Code: NotFound
   at Anthropic.AnthropicClientWithRawResponse.Execute[T](...)
   ...
(core dumped)  [exit code: 134]
```

**Verified after the fix**, same commands:

```
--- Technical ---
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v1.1.0' failed: anthropic at http://127.0.0.1:8799/v1/messages answered 404 Not Found for model 'claude-sonnet-5'.
           Either the endpoint does not serve that model id (check llm.model), or Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl is not the address of this provider's API - another provider's, or a wrong path such as a missing /v1.
           The endpoint said: model: claude-sonnet-5

--- Customer ---
  (failed) The same as Technical.
```
```
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v1.1.0' failed: openai-compatible at http://127.0.0.1:8799/v1/chat/completions answered 401 Unauthorized for model 'gpt-luna'.
           The endpoint rejected the key in OPENAI_API_KEY: it is expired, revoked or mistyped, or it is another provider's key.
           The endpoint said: Incorrect API key provided: sk-dummy.
```
```
  Flagged for review:
    ! The thorough check could not be evaluated: anthropic at http://127.0.0.1:8799/v1/messages answered 404 Not Found for model 'check-model'.
      Either the endpoint does not serve that model id (check faithfulness.model), or Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl is not the address of this provider's API - another provider's, or a wrong path such as a missing /v1.
      The endpoint said: model: check-model.
```
Also checked: openai-compatible 404 and anthropic 401, a 401 with `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset (`The endpoint needs a key, and OPENAI_API_KEY is not set.`), and a refused connection for both providers.

changes.title: fix(llm): refuse a base URL that belongs to another provider's API
changes.description:
Closes #233

- **Refused at config load, not warned:** a `Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl` whose host belongs to another provider's API stops the run before the history is read, so the key never leaves the machine. The run header already named the mismatch and nothing stopped on it; a key that went out has to be rotated.
- **Two hosts, both certain:** `api.openai.com` is refused for `anthropic`, `api.anthropic.com` for `openai-compatible`. Every other host is accepted, because a proxy or a gateway lives at a host of its own. The list stays short on purpose: several hosted endpoints serve both dialects under one host, so a longer one would refuse working setups.
- **Names both settings, and says when the provider was not set:** `llm.provider is not set and defaults to 'anthropic'` is how the mismatch happens - the endpoint came from the environment, the provider from a `chartula.yaml` in another repository. The key variable named is the one in force, not the default.
- **Checked where the options are read** (`ReadOptions`), so the refusal holds wherever they are read, not only where the client is built. It lives in `ProviderHost`, beside `EndpointUrl`.
- `api.anthropic.com` also serves an OpenAI-compatible layer, which `openai-compatible` can no longer reach; the refusal points at `llm.provider: anthropic`, the adapter that speaks Anthropic's API in full.
- Docs: `configuration.md` (environment-only settings).

**Reproduced before the fix** with the release binary, a dummy key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-dummy`) and a local GitHub stub, the way the issue was found - the dummy key went to `api.openai.com`:

```
Model:  anthropic at https://api.openai.com/v1, key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
        claude-sonnet-5, thinking provider-default
...
--- Technical ---
  (failed) Changelog generation for 'v1.1.0' failed: Status Code: NotFound
```

**Verified after the fix**, same command, also with networking disabled (`unshare -rn`), exit code 1:

```
Configuration error: Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl 'https://api.openai.com/v1' is OpenAI's API, but llm.provider is not set and defaults to 'anthropic', so the key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY would be sent to OpenAI. For OpenAI's API, set llm.provider to openai-compatible (in chartula.yaml, or as Chartula__Llm__Provider); otherwise unset Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl.
```

and the other direction:

```
Configuration error: Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl 'https://api.anthropic.com/v1' is Anthropic's API, but llm.provider is 'openai-compatible', so the key in OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to Anthropic. For Anthropic's API, set llm.provider to anthropic (in chartula.yaml, or as Chartula__Llm__Provider); otherwise unset Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl.
```

Tests: `LlmWiringTests` (provider not set, both directions, host spelled in upper case with a trailing dot, renamed key variable, gateways and matching hosts accepted), `ForeignProviderHostTests` (the built CLI stops before any request); full suite 742 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(faithfulness): let the thorough check run on its own model and thinking mode
changes.description:
Follows #231, point 5 of the measurement plan for the provider comparison runs

- **`faithfulness.model` and `faithfulness.thinking`:** the thorough check can ask its own model and reason at its own level, at the same provider, endpoint and key. Unset, each falls back to `llm`. Rendering writes prose and the check answers a short verdict, so a cheaper model can do one and a stronger one the other; thinking is separate because on the check it has been measured to cost thousands of output tokens without finding more.
- **No second client:** the model is sent per call as `ChatOptions.ModelId`, which both adapters honor (checked against the real SDKs: the request body carries the override). `ChatModelOptions` gains `CheckModelId` and `CheckReasoning`; `ChatModel` picks per operation.
- **Resolved in one place:** `ThoroughCheckModel` resolves model and thinking from `faithfulness`, then `llm`. The request, the run header and the provenance all read it, so they cannot disagree.
- **Refusals name the key in force:** a Claude combination known to fail is refused at config load as `faithfulness.thinking 'high' is not supported by faithfulness.model 'claude-haiku-4-5'`, or with the `llm.*` key when the check inherits it.
- **Provenance:** `checkModel` and `checkThinking`, recorded resolved, also when they repeat the rendering's, and only when the check ran. Additive under `schemaVersion: 1`; the run record carries the same provenance.
- **Run header:** a `thorough check: <model>, thinking <mode>` line, only when it differs from the rendering.
- Metrics already separate the operations, so each model's tokens and time are on their own line.
- Docs: `configuration.md` (faithfulness), `changelog-json.md`, `run-record.md`, `chartula.example.yaml`.

**Verified end to end:** the release binary on six real Chartula commits against a local OpenAI-compatible fake that logs each request, with `llm: gpt-luna, disabled` and `faithfulness: gpt-sol, high`:

```
Model:  openai-compatible at http://127.0.0.1:8766/v1, key from OPENAI_API_KEY
        gpt-luna, thinking disabled
        thorough check: gpt-sol, thinking high
```
Requests the endpoint received: `render model=gpt-luna effort=none`, `check model=gpt-sol effort=high`.

Tests: `ThoroughCheckModelTests` (inheritance, own model and thinking, refusal by key, wire test through both real adapters, provenance resolved and absent when off, run header); `ProvenanceWiringTests` adapted; full suite 732 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(observability): say how much release a run worked on
changes.description:
Follows #230, point 4 of the measurement plan for the provider comparison runs

- **The context for every token count:** the summary opens with `Release: 14 commits, 10 pull requests, 9 facts (7 with a description, 22,512 characters)`, and the run record carries the same as `metrics.release`. Comparing runs across repositories needs it: cost follows description length more than pull request count (the README's alpha runs: about 22,500 vs 230 characters for ten pull requests each).
- **Counted where the facts are established:** the pipeline records the scope right after the fact base is built - commits in the range, merged pull requests behind them, facts after filtering.
- **Characters are what the model reads:** the facts' descriptions, after template comments are stripped and at the configured `factBase.depth` - `title-only` counts 0, because nothing beyond the title is sent. Titles are left out: short, and roughly proportional to the fact count already shown.
- Recorded through `IRunMetrics.RecordReleaseScope`, so the summary and the record read it from one `RunReport`. Additive under `schemaVersion: 1`.
- Docs: `run-metrics.md`, `run-record.md`.

**Verified end to end:** the release binary on six real Chartula commits (GitHub read with a token), against a local fake model:

```
  Release:          6 commits, 6 pull requests, 4 facts (4 with a description, 9,902 characters)
```

Tests: `ReleasePipelineMetricsTests` (scope recorded from the stubbed release), `RunReportFormatterTests` (line, absent without scope), `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests` (written and read back); full suite 725 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(observability): show the cached input and the reasoning inside a run's tokens
changes.description:
Follows #229 (`LlmCall` record), point 3 of the measurement plan for the provider comparison runs

- **Two parts of the tokens made visible:** cached input (served from the provider's prompt cache, usually billed lower) and reasoning output (spent thinking, billed as output, never in the changelog). Both come from `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`'s `UsageDetails`, so no provider type is named.
- **Checked what each adapter fills, against the real SDKs:**

  | | input | cached | reasoning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Anthropic | includes cache reads | `cache_read_input_tokens` | not reported (folded into output) |
  | OpenAI | `prompt_tokens` | `cached_tokens` | `reasoning_tokens` |

  Same meaning on both: cached is a part of input, reasoning a part of output, so `in / out` stay complete totals.
- **Not reported stays unknown:** summed over the calls that reported it, `null` until one does; the summary says `reasoning not reported` rather than 0, which would claim the model did not think.
- Cache writes (Anthropic's `cache_creation_input_tokens`) are left out: they arrive only under an adapter-specific key, and occur only when caching is requested, which Chartula does not do today.
- **Summary:** a `of which N in cached, M out reasoning` line under each operation with calls. **Run record:** `cachedInputTokens`, `reasoningTokens` per operation, left out when not reported; additive under `schemaVersion: 1`.
- Docs: `run-metrics.md`, `run-record.md`.

**Verified end to end:** the release binary against a local OpenAI-compatible fake reporting both details:

```
  Rephrasing:       1 call, 6,000 in / 320 out, 0.5 s
    of which 4,096 in cached, 300 out reasoning
```

Tests: `UsageDetailTests` (real Anthropic and OpenAI adapters), `RunMetricsTests` (summing with unreported calls), `RunReportFormatterTests` (detail line, not reported), `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests` (written and omitted); full suite 721 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(observability): record how long each model call took and how often it was retried
changes.description:
Closes #128

- **Time per call, per operation, per run:** `ChatModel` times every model call, retries included, and the pipeline times the run from reading history to the last model call. The summary shows each operation's total and its longest call - one slow call and uniformly slow calls call for different fixes - and the run's total next to its tokens.
- **Retries counted from the wire, for every provider:** both provider SDKs retry on their own through the `HttpClient` they are given. A `DelegatingHandler` under each client (`ModelRequestCountingHandler`) reports every request to a counter that flows with the call's async context (`Core/Llm/ModelCallAttempts`); requests beyond the first are retries. No provider type is named in the domain, and a client Chartula did not build reports nothing, which reads as `not observed`, never as zero.
- **Failed calls recorded, not lost:** a call that throws is recorded as failed with its time and requests, then rethrown. Its time counts, it is kept out of `calls` (which counts answers) and out of the unreported-usage lower bound.
- **SDK timeouts unchanged:** the supplied `HttpClient` has an infinite timeout, as the SDKs' own clients do (checked by reflection); both SDKs still enforce their own timeout through it (checked with a slow stub: OpenAI `NetworkTimeout` and Anthropic `Timeout` both fire at 1 s).
- **`LlmCall` record:** `IRunMetrics.RecordLlmCall` takes one record (tokens, duration, attempts, failed) instead of loose counts, so the next usage fields (reasoning and cached tokens) are additions, not signature changes.
- **Run record:** `failedCalls`, `durationSeconds`, `longestCallSeconds`, `retries` (left out when not observed) per operation, and `durationSeconds` for the run. Additive under `schemaVersion: 1`; a record written before reads with zeros.
- Docs: `run-metrics.md` (new "When a run was slow"), `run-record.md`. `parked` removed from #128.

**Verified end to end:** the release binary against a local OpenAI-compatible fake that answers the first request with 503 and the next after 1.5 s:

```
  Rephrasing:       1 call, 6,000 in / 20 out, 1.7 s
  Total:            6,020 tokens in 4.6 s
  Retries:          1 (rephrasing 1)
```

Tests: `ModelCallTimingTests` (late answer, failed call, retries from reported requests, not observed without a transport), `ModelRequestCountingTests` (real Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs retrying once through the handler, first-time answer is 0 not unknown, infinite client timeout), `RunMetricsTests`, `RunReportFormatterTests`, `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests` (fields, omission, older records), `ReleasePipelineMetricsTests` (run duration); full suite 715 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(llm): one thinking setting for every provider
changes.description:
Closes #87

- **One vocabulary, every provider:** `llm.thinking` is `provider-default`, `disabled`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh`. Chartula sends it as `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`'s provider-neutral `ChatOptions.Reasoning`, and each adapter translates it itself. Checked against the real adapters with the network stubbed:

  | `thinking` | Anthropic | OpenAI / compatible |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `provider-default` | nothing sent | nothing sent |
  | `disabled` | `thinking: disabled` | `reasoning_effort: none` |
  | `low` ... `xhigh` | `thinking: adaptive` + `output_config.effort` | `reasoning_effort` at that level |

- **OpenAI-compatible is no longer refused:** before, anything but `provider-default` failed at config load there. An endpoint whose model does not reason, or does not know a level, answers the first request with an error; its model ids say nothing reliable to check in advance.
- **The Anthropic raw-request fragment is gone:** `ChatModelOptions.RawRepresentationFactory` becomes `Reasoning`. The fragment had to repeat the model and the output ceiling because the adapter took it as given; the neutral path keeps both (asserted in the adapter test). `AnthropicThinking` shrinks to `ClaudeThinkingSupport`, the config-load check.
- **Config-load check for Claude:** an effort level needs Claude 4.6+, `xhigh` needs Opus 4.7+ (refused on the 4.6 models), `disabled` stays refused on Fable. Unreadable ids pass through, as before.
- **`adaptive` and `on` read as `high`:** adaptive thinking without an effort is high effort, so existing files ask for what they asked for. Provenance and the run record now show `high` for them.
- **What ran is shown:** the run header names the model and the resolved mode (`claude-sonnet-5, thinking high`), the same name the provenance records.
- **A regression test on the wire:** `One_value_asks_every_provider_for_the_same_thing` drives both real adapters and reads the request bodies. The mapping lives in the provider packages, so an update that changed it fails here instead of on the invoice.
- Docs: `configuration.md` (mapping table, which refusals happen when), README Configuration, `changelog-json.md`, `chartula.example.yaml`.

**Verified end to end:** the release binary with `provider: openai-compatible` and `thinking: disabled` / `high` loads the configuration (refused before), reads GitHub and reaches the model call; an unknown value is still refused by name. Header:

```
Model:  openai-compatible at http://127.0.0.1:9/v1, key from OPENAI_API_KEY
        gpt-test, thinking high
```

Not verified against a live model: which levels GPT models accept is the endpoint's answer, and the comparison runs are next.

Tests: `ThinkingModeTests` rewritten (levels, legacy aliases, adapter wire test for all six values, Claude refusals), `LlmWiringTests` (OpenAI-compatible carries the effort), `ChatModelTests` (reasoning passed through), `EndpointNoticeTests` (resolved mode shown), `ProvenanceWiringTests` (every level reads back); full suite 695 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat: keep a run's metrics in a local run record
changes.description:
Closes #224
Follows #225 (the record carries the settings it added)

- **A file per `generate` run, `chartula-runs/<UTC time>-<tag>.json`:** the run metrics as the summary prints them (calls and tokens per operation, both checks' activity, `onlyThoroughFlags`, `notEvaluated`), the provenance, each audience's flags or error, the time, repository and mode. Two runs compare from their files alone.
- **One file per run, not appended:** each record is a whole JSON document to read and diff on its own, and no run rewrites an earlier one. The time comes first so the files list in run order; two runs in the same second get `-2`, `-3`; a tag's `/` becomes `-`.
- **Never published:** usage is a fact about the run, not the release, so `changelog.json` and the release notes are untouched. `docs/run-record.md` says to ignore `/chartula-runs/`, and this repository does.
- **Provenance in `changelog.json`'s own fields:** `ChangelogJsonSerializer.ToDocument` is shared, so a record and the file its run wrote match without a second source.
- **Versioned apart:** its own `schemaVersion: 1` and Stability section, documented like `changelog.json`.
- **`preview` writes no record:** its promise is to write nothing.
- **A run in which nothing rendered is recorded:** its tokens were spent. `changelog.json` is still held back then.
- **Written before the other outputs:** every model call is done by then, so the record is complete, and it does not depend on publishing succeeding.
- **Operations with no calls are zeros, a failed audience has no `flags`:** a zero is a value that compares; an empty list would read as a clean check.
- The run summary names the file under its metrics: `Recorded in <path>`.
- Escaping (`+`, `'`) follows `changelog.json`; whether both should relax is #226.

**Verified, release build:** `generate --no-publish --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --since v0.1.0-preview.1~2` on this repository with an invalid `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (no tokens spent): both audiences fail with 401, exit 1, the summary ends with `Recorded in .../chartula-runs/20260922T144044Z-v0.1.0-preview.1.json`, the file holds both errors, zeroed metrics and the full provenance, and git ignores it.
Not verified end-to-end: a run that renders, which needs a paid model run; covered by the pipeline and serializer tests.

Tests: 6 new in `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests`, 4 in `RunRecordPipelineTests` (generate and --no-publish record, preview does not, a run with nothing rendered does), 4 in `FileRunRecordWriterTests` (name, same second, slash in tag, provenance), 2 in `ReleaseCommandMetricsTests`, 1 assertion in `OutputWiringTests`; full suite 677 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: feat(serialization): record thinking, the thorough check and the fact base depth in changelog.json
changes.description:
Closes #223
Follows #202

- **Three settings added to `provenance`:** `thinking`, `thoroughCheck`, `factBaseDepth`. They move a run's cost and output most, and the docs' measurements were taken with them from memory; a file now says what it was made with.
- **Spelled as the configuration spells them:** `provider-default` / `disabled` / `adaptive`, and `title-only` / `title-and-description` / `title-description-and-issues`. `ThinkingModeParser.Name` and `FactBaseDepthParser.Name` give the canonical name; tests read each one back through `Parse`, so an alias like `off` is recorded as `disabled`.
- **Unset thinking is recorded as `provider-default`, not left out:** it is a setting with a meaning. The docs say it records the setting, not whether the model thought - some models think by default.
- **`thoroughCheck: false` is written:** a boolean false is a value; only a setting the run does not have is left out, as for every provenance field.
- **Additive under `schemaVersion: 1`**, as the Stability section allows. The stored fixtures carry no provenance, so none needed regenerating.
- **Composition:** `AddChartulaOutputs` reads the faithfulness and fact-base options the same way their own `Add*` do; nothing is registered twice.
- Tokens stay out of this file (it is published); a local run record is #224.

**Verified:** build and `dotnet format` clean; no end-to-end `generate`, which needs a paid model run - the writer path is covered by the serialization and wiring tests.

Tests: 2 new in `ProvenanceSerializationTests` (fields written and read back, unset fields left out), 8 in `ProvenanceWiringTests` (settings recorded, unset thinking as `provider-default`, names read back as themselves); full suite 661 passing.

changes.title: docs: drop the wrong $1.78 figure and record what the thorough check costs
changes.description:
Closes #176

- **The $1.78 figure is gone:** it was wrong, and "under review" kept a wrong number in the docs where it read as a cost. The 2026-09-17 Sonnet 5 table ($0.25-0.29) stays as the figure for this repository's release.
- **The thorough check's cost, from runs that already exist:** the three alpha runs in the README ran with the check on, and the run metrics report its tokens apart from rephrasing, so the run without it is the total minus that line - no second run needed. It took 29%, 29% and 45% of the tokens of runs that cost about $0.06, $0.07 and $0.20.
- **Default stays on (OD13):** a few cents per run, and on Ingestor `v3.2.0` it caught the one invented claim the rule-based check missed (the README example).
- **"A run pays per token twice over" reworded:** it read as if the check doubled the cost; it is one more call per audience, a minority of the tokens.

**Verified:** percentages from the README table (3,256 / 11,167; 3,591 / 12,371; 24,017 / 53,129); no other mention of $1.78 in the repository.

Tests: none, docs only.

changes.title: fix: report a refused publication next to the files the run wrote
changes.description:
Closes #219
Follows #218

- **A refusal names the write, not the tag:** a 401/403/404 on publishing says GitHub refused to publish the release notes for the tag to the repository, whether a token was sent, and that publishing needs Contents read and write. GitHub's named permission (`x-accepted-github-permissions`) is quoted when present. The pull requests were read a moment earlier, so a refusal here is about writing - most likely the read-only token the docs recommend until a run publishes.
- **No raw JSON:** every other error quotes GitHub's `message` field, against the tag instead of an API path (`repos/.../releases/42`).
- **The files survive the error:** publishing is the last write, so the pipeline catches its `InvalidOperationException` (the port's documented failure) and returns it as `ReleaseOutcome.PublishFailure` next to `WrittenOutputs`. Before, the exception dropped the list and the run printed only the error.
- **Output and exit code:** the summary lists "Wrote:", then "Not published: the release notes." with the reason and what a re-run costs: it replaces this release's `CHANGELOG.md` section and draft rather than adding to them (checked in `ChangelogMarkdownComposer`), but pays for the model calls again. Exit code 1, as for a failed audience.
- **One reading of GitHub errors:** `GitHub/GitHubErrorResponse` holds what #218 put in the pull request reader (message, token sent, named permission, rate limit), now shared by both adapters. A 401 counts as a rejected token only when one was sent; without one it is the missing token.
- The writer takes the token variable from the composition root, as the reader does since #218.
- `docs/cli.md`: what a refused publication leaves behind.

**Verified:** the real `GitHubReleaseNotesWriter` against `api.github.com` without a token (nothing can be written that way):

```
Error: GitHub refused to publish the release notes for v9.9.9 to goldbarth/chartula (401 Unauthorized).
  The request carried no token: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set.
  Publishing needs a token with Contents read and write on goldbarth/chartula.
```

Not verified end-to-end: the full `generate` run up to the refusal (needs a paid model run) and the 403 with a real read-only token; both covered by tests, the token case comes with the token-permission check still pending.

Tests: 3 new in `GitHubReleaseNotesWriterTests` (read-only token with named permission, no token, other error in GitHub's words), 1 in `ReleasePipelineTests` (refusal keeps the written files), 1 in `ReleaseCommandOutputTests` (listing, message, exit code 1); full suite 651 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: fix(history): name the checkout and its tags when the release tag is not there
changes.description:
Closes #146

- **Outside any repository, its own message:** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` decides; the message names the directory and says to run from a checkout of the repository the release belongs to.
- **Wrong checkout or missing tag, named by place:** the message names the checkout root git reports (also correct when the run starts in a subdirectory) and asks for a checkout of the right repository with its tags fetched (`git fetch --tags`).
- **The newest three tags, or "It has no tags.":** a typo or a different naming scheme (`1.3.0` vs `v1.3.0`) shows at a glance; no tags at all is a clone that never fetched them, the case the old message hid best.
- The extra git calls run only on the failure path; a run whose tag resolves reads the same as before.
- `TempGitRepository.Run` returns git's output, so the test compares against the root git itself reports (`/private/var` on macOS, forward slashes on Windows) instead of rebuilding the path.

**Repro, release build** (`preview --tag v1.3.0 --repo goldbarth/foo`):

| Started in | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | `Tag 'v1.3.0' does not resolve to a commit in the repository.` | `'/' is not inside a git repository.` + run from a checkout |
| chartula clone | same | `Tag 'v1.3.0' is not in the checkout at /home/.../chartula.` + `Its latest tags: v0.1.0-preview.1.` + `git fetch --tags` |
| fresh repo, no tags | same | same, with `It has no tags.` |
| `chartula/src` | same | names the checkout root, not `src` |

Tests: 3 new in `GitCliCommitReaderTests` (latest tags named, no tags, outside a repository); full suite 640 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: fix(pull-requests): name the repository and the token, not a commit, when GitHub refuses access
changes.description:
Closes #149

- **Repository, not commit, on the first request:** a 403 or 404 before anything was read is about `--repo` or the credentials, so the message names the repository and the likely causes (misspelled `--repo`, private repository without a token that can read it). A later 404 stays a commit problem, since the repository was readable a request earlier.
- **Says whether a token was sent:** both real cases in the issue comment were a token problem the message did not name. The message now says "no token: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set" or "the token from GITHUB_TOKEN", and quotes `x-accepted-github-permissions` (e.g. `pull_requests=read`) when GitHub names the missing permission.
- **Wrong checkout is a 422, not a 404:** checked against the API; a repository that exists but does not hold the commit answers `422 No commit found for SHA`. That case gets its own message: not a checkout of `--repo`, or the commit is not pushed.
- **401 and a spent rate limit named as such:** a rejected token says expired, revoked or mistyped; a 403/429 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` says the budget is spent, not that access is missing - the startup notice from #110 already predicts that failure.
- **No raw JSON:** every remaining error quotes GitHub's `message` field; the body is the fallback only when it is not JSON.
- **Variable name from the composition root:** the reader takes the token variable as a constructor argument instead of assuming `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so the message stays true when it is renamed.

Not in here: `GitHubReleaseNotesWriter` has the same raw-JSON pattern when publishing; separate issue.

**Repro, release build against the real API** (`preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.1 --since <sha>`):

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--repo` does not exist, no token | `404 Not Found for commit 8930f18... {"message":"Not Found",...}` | `GitHub cannot read goldbarth/does-not-exist-xyz (404 Not Found).` + no token + likely causes |
| `--repo` does not exist, token set | same | same header, "carried the token from GITHUB_TOKEN", token cannot read it or lacks Pull requests (read) |
| Bogus token | raw 401 JSON | `GitHub rejected the token in GITHUB_TOKEN (401 Unauthorized): it is expired, revoked or mistyped.` |
| Run in chartula, `--repo goldbarth/chartula-evals` | raw 422 JSON | `Commit 8930f18... is not in goldbarth/chartula-evals on GitHub (422 ...)` + checkout or unpushed |

Tests: 6 new in `GitHubPullRequestReaderTests` (404 first request, 403 with permission header, later 404, 422, 401, rate limit); full suite 643 passing, build and `dotnet format` clean.

changes.title: docs: move the roadmap and what is out of scope into ROADMAP.md
changes.description:
Follows #164 (board aligned with the roadmap order)

- **Roadmap out of the README:** the ordered list moves to `ROADMAP.md`; the README keeps one line under Status that links to it. The README is too long to skim, and a plan changes on its own schedule, not the README's.

changes.title: feat(repo): install with one command on Linux, macOS and Windows
changes.description:
Follows #208 (part of #181, R58: a two-minute path at launch)

- **Why:** downloading the binary leaves the steps that stall a first install: picking the architecture, `chmod +x`, renaming, putting it on the PATH, Gatekeeper. For someone new to the terminal that can take an hour. Now it is one line:
  - Linux, macOS: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goldbarth/chartula/main/install.sh | sh`
  - Windows: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goldbarth/chartula/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- **`install.sh` (POSIX sh, curl or wget):** detects OS and architecture (the native binary under Rosetta; a clear stop on musl, whose missing glibc would otherwise fail without saying why), downloads the binary and `SHA256SUMS`, installs only on a matching checksum, runs `--help` once, puts it at `~/.local/bin/chartula`. It changes no shell file: if the directory is not on the PATH it prints the one line to add for the user's shell. A file fetched by curl carries no quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper does not block it.
- **`install.ps1` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7):** the same, into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\chartula`, and it **does** add that folder to the user PATH (user scope only) and to the running session, because editing PATH by hand is the Windows stall. It never calls `exit`, which under `irm | iex` would close the user's window; errors end in one plain message.
- Both scripts run from a function body, so a download cut off halfway executes nothing.
- **No API:** the scripts download through `releases/latest/download/<file>`, a web redirect without the API's 60 requests an hour. Found while testing: the API answered 403 from this IP after a Chartula run had used the budget, and a user behind a shared IP would have hit the same wall. That link resolves only a release GitHub counts as latest, so `release.yml` no longer marks releases as pre-releases; `-preview.N` in the version says it already. `docs/versioning.md` updated.
- **`install.yml`:** runs both scripts the way a user does, on all six platforms (and Windows PowerShell 5.1 next to 7), when a script changes and whenever a release is published, so a release that cannot be installed shows up at once.
- `CHARTULA_VERSION`, `CHARTULA_INSTALL_DIR` and `CHARTULA_DOWNLOAD_URL` (a mirror or local copy) are optional overrides.

**Verified locally (Linux) against the real `v0.1.0-preview.1` assets served from a local copy:** `install.sh` installs, the checksum passes, `--help` runs, the PATH hint names `~/.zshrc`; a tampered `SHA256SUMS` installs nothing; piped through `sh` like `curl | sh`. `install.ps1` under PowerShell 7.6 on Linux: tampered checksum and 404 each end in one message with the session alive; the happy path installs and checks the binary. Windows-only parts (user PATH, `.exe`) are covered by this PR's `install.ps1 (...)` checks, which need `v0.1.0-preview.1` published.

Tests: `install.yml` (4 unix runners, 2 Windows runners x 2 PowerShells); shellcheck and actionlint clean.

changes.title: docs: show what Chartula produces, what it costs and where it stops
changes.description:
Closes #182
Closes #90
Refs #183 (the README roadmap; the chartula-evals README follows in its own repository)

- **Positioned as a check layer** between merged pull requests and published release communication, not as another changelog generator. The .NET badge is gone: the binary needs no .NET, and the badge filtered readers who do not use it.
- **A fact next to its customer entry, from a foreign run:** Ingestor `v3.2.0` #180. The fact is a branch-name title with no description; the customer entry invents a rename and tells customers to act on it; the thorough check flags exactly that. One example shows both claims, and it says openly that the free rule-based check missed it.
- **Claims restated to what holds:** "cannot invent a change" is worded to what `RenderingComposer.FindMismatch` enforces (one entry per fact, or the audience fails); "reports what it could not verify"; "no hosting, no subscription" instead of "costs you nothing". A fourth point says the facts are author text, so the tool does not make a wrong pull request true.
- **Cost per run from the three Phase 2 runs:** measured tokens, and a dollar figure computed at the Sonnet 5 rate already documented in `docs/configuration.md`, labelled as not billed. No billed amounts exist per run, since one key served all three. Cost follows description length, not pull request count (about 22,500 vs 230 characters).
- **Known limitations:** everything the alpha leaves for later, plus one seen in the Ingestor run: two pull requests with the same change become two entries.
- **Credentials for every provider** (#90): a table for `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`, and a local server without a key; setup stays in `docs/configuration.md`.
- **Install is a placeholder:** download, checksum and `PATH` land with the first preview release (#181). Build from source sits below it as the second way.
- **Roadmap** matches the alpha scope and lists what comes after it in order; webhooks, widget and RSS move to "Out of scope (for now)".
- Links the alpha feedback form (#212).

**Verified against the run artifacts:** every quoted fact, entry, flag and token count is copied from the stored `changelog.json` and run output of Ingestor `v3.2.0`, port-tidewatch `v1.3.0` and ServiceDeskLite `v1.9.0` (toolVersion `0.1.0-alpha+873b7a4`, `claude-sonnet-5`). No new run.

### What's New

- **Installing on Alpine:** You can now install and run Chartula on Alpine, with binaries available for x64 and arm64. Install libstdc++ first with apk add libstdc++; the installer will tell you if it is missing and will not install anything until you do.
- **Thorough check model:** The thorough check can now use a different model and thinking mode from the one used to write the changelog. You can rely on the run header and provenance to show which model and mode the check used; set them under faithfulness in chartula.yaml.
- **Release scope in metrics:** The run summary and local run record now show how many commits, pull requests and facts a release covered, along with the length of the fact descriptions. You can use that scope when comparing token use across runs.
- **Token breakdown:** Run metrics now show cached input tokens and reasoning output tokens when the provider reports them. You can distinguish those portions from the total input and output tokens without treating an unreported value as zero.
- **Call timing and retries:** Run metrics now show each operation's time, longest model call and observed retries, plus the run's total time. You can see whether time was spent in a long call or across the run; retries remain marked as unobserved when Chartula cannot count them.
- **Thinking modes:** You can now choose the same thinking modes for Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible providers. The run header shows the mode used, so you can check it before comparing runs; set llm.thinking in chartula.yaml.
- **Local run records:** Each generate run now writes its metrics, settings and results to a separate JSON file in chartula-runs; preview still writes no record. You can compare runs from their local files without putting usage details in published release notes.
- **Recorded generation settings:** The provenance in changelog.json now includes the thinking mode, whether the thorough check was enabled and the fact-base depth. You can check those settings in the file when reviewing how a changelog was made.
- **One-command installation:** You can now install Chartula with one command on Linux, macOS or Windows. The installer selects the binary and checks its checksum, so you no longer have to choose and place the download yourself.

### Bug Fixes

- **Shallow checkout history:** A shallow checkout could be mistaken for a first release or leave part of a release's history unread. Chartula now refuses an incomplete range rather than using it; fetch the full history with git fetch --unshallow --tags, use fetch-depth: 0 in GitHub Actions, or set GIT_DEPTH: 0 in GitLab CI.
- **Starting in slim containers:** Chartula could stop at startup in slim Linux containers without ICU. You can now run the Linux binary there without installing ICU.
- **Configuration file errors:** A malformed chartula.yaml could crash Chartula or leave a setting unused without warning. Errors now name the file, line and column, so you can correct the configuration before running again.
- **Model call errors:** A failed model call could leave you with an unclear error, and a failed thorough check could stop the run. Errors now identify the provider, endpoint, model and response, so you can see what to check while a failed thorough check leaves the rendering available for review.
- **Provider endpoint mismatch:** A configured endpoint belonging to another provider could receive the key for the selected provider. Chartula now refuses that combination before sending the key; correct llm.provider in chartula.yaml or unset Chartula__Llm__BaseUrl.
- **Publication refusals:** GitHub could refuse to publish release notes after Chartula had written the output files, without the summary listing them. The summary now names those files and the publication error, so you can use the written output; rerun publishing with a token that has Contents read and write permission.
- **Missing release tag:** A release tag that was missing from the current checkout produced an error without identifying where Chartula was running. The error now names the checkout and its latest tags, so you can check whether you are in the right repository; fetch its tags with git fetch --tags if they are missing.
- **GitHub access errors:** A GitHub access refusal could point to a commit instead of the repository or token involved. The error now names the repository, whether a token was sent and any permission GitHub reports, so you can check the repository and credentials.
